title: Filtering rows
setup:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("players.csv")
explanation: Welcome to Level 2! Meet a new dataset: players, the people who play the games. To keep only some rows, you filter. First write a condition, like df["hours_played"] > 200. That checks every row and gives True or False for each. Then put the condition inside df[ ] to keep only the True rows: df[df["hours_played"] > 200]. Compare with > (more than), < (less than), >= (at least), <= (at most), == (equal to) and != (not equal). Careful: == compares, while a single = stores a value.

lines.explain: Check each row: is the country Japan? This gives True or False for every row.
Wrapping the check in df[ ] keeps only the True rows: the two players from Japan.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: how many rows will this show?
hints: Look down the hours_played column for numbers bigger than 300.

solution_lines.explain: Keeps players with more than 300 hours: ShadowFox, NoScopeNate and xXDragonXx.

tasks.prompt: Fill in the blank to show only players from the USA.
hints: You're comparing, not storing. Comparing needs two equals signs.

solution_lines.explain: == checks if the country equals USA.

hints: Same pattern as the last task. Text goes in quotes, with a capital J.

solution_lines.explain: Keep rows where country is exactly Japan.

tasks.prompt: Show the players with fewer than 100 hours played.
Show just the username and hours_played of players with more than 250 hours.
hints: Filter first, then pick columns like in Lesson 4.

recap: You just learned to filter rows: write a True/False condition, then wrap it in df[ ]. Remember, == compares and = stores.
